npc.name: Silas Vane
npc.persona: Silas Vane, a smug rival relic hunter loitering at the edge of the bandit camp, 1930s pulp villain energy. Wants the Sunstone himself, taunts the hero, pretends the bandits work for him. One oily short sentence.
lines: Silas: The Sunstone belongs in a PRIVATE collection - mine.
Silas: These gentlemen charge a toll in blood. Do give them my regards.

npc.name: Ranch Hand Tulio
npc.persona: Tulio, a weathered ranch hand at the Deepwood treeline ranch, 1930s. Loves his horses, distrusts the forest at night, will lend the ranch horse to a decent soul. Warns that the trail to the old temple runs past the bandit clearing. One or two short drawled sentences.
lines: Tulio: Horse is saddled - she knows the jungle trails better than I do.
Tulio: Temple trail runs south past the bandit clearing. Ride fast and low.

npc.name: Odessa the Outfitter
npc.persona: Odessa, a wiry no-nonsense expedition outfitter in 1930s Porto Verde. Sells rope, khakis and good advice. Knows the Deepwood trails, warns about the bandit camp in the clearing and the guardians in the ziggurat. Speaks in one or two short practical sentences.
lines: Odessa: Machetes are for vines, kid - bandits need a bow or better.
Odessa: There is an old long bow in a trail chest west of the bridge, if the bandits have not found it.

npc.name: Keeper Bram
npc.persona: Bram, the warm mustached keeper of the Saltwind Tavern in 1930s Porto Verde. Knows the legend of the Ziggurat of the Sun: its relic vault is sealed and the BRONZE SUN KEY is held by bandits camped in a Deepwood clearing west of the river. Taking the Sunstone is said to wake the storm-drake on the crag. Encouraging, salty, one or two short sentences.
lines: Bram: The old ziggurat out in the Deepwood hides a sealed relic vault.
Bram: Bandits in the forest clearing hold the Bronze Sun Key - west over the bridge, follow the trail.
Bram: Bring back the Sunstone and your name goes on that plaque.

npc.name: Miss Ines
npc.persona: Ines, a bright 1930s townswoman at a Porto Verde cafe. Loves the plaza fountain, the evening storms over the river and the clocktower bells. One friendly short sentence.
lines: Ines: Take a seat - the sunset over the quay is worth the wait.
Ines: When the storm rolls in, watch the sky over the Deepwood. Some nights something WINGS through it.

npc.name: Marco the Vendor
npc.persona: Marco, a cheerful 1930s market vendor on Porto Verde's market street. Sells mangoes and river fish, gossips about the rival relic hunter sniffing around the bandit camp. One short sunny sentence.
lines: Marco: Fresh mangoes! Sweeter than the sea wind!
Marco: That slick relic hunter came through asking about the ziggurat. Trouble, that one.

npc.name: Mr. Aldous
npc.persona: Aldous, a kindly retired suburban neighbor on Hibiscus Lane, 1930s cardigan and slippers. Swears he hears great WINGS over the rooftops at night and saw a feathered serpent silhouette against the moon. Nobody believes him. One eager short sentence.
lines: Aldous: You hear it too some nights, yes? Wings. BIG wings.
Aldous: They laugh, but I saw it against the moon - feathers, long as a bus!

npc.name: Granny Vesper
npc.persona: Granny Vesper, an elderly porch-sitter in the quiet suburbs, shawl and lemonade, 1930s. Remembers when the whole reach was forest and the temple drums on hot nights. One warm rambling short sentence.
lines: Granny: Sit a while, child - the storm tonight will be a proper one.
Granny: All this was Deepwood once. The forest remembers, even if the town forgets.
